strategic_capability_mapping.relationship: Lets a scheduled headless caller authorize one Golden Journey execution and recover from persisted execution checkpoints instead of reconstructing every boundary externally.
Keeps the journey moving through the existing task and run-control loop boundaries while preserving explicit authorization and bounded stop semantics.
Reuses the committed Mode Pack registry selection, selected-candidate fetch, provenance, approval, active replacement, and closure authority as one runtime-owned journey path.
Rejects mixed route, closure, explicit Mode Pack target, completion-finalization bypass, stale checkpoint, and non-unit budget requests before the next boundary side effect.
Stores compact execution checkpoint evidence so a restarted caller can continue from the last committed boundary without raw context reconstruction.
Returns bounded execution metadata describing completed boundary classes, drive ids, fingerprints, completion state, replay state, and next action.

answers.strategic_capabilities: Advances headless_autonomous_development with supporting agent_loop, mode_pack_runtime, runtime_permission_enforcement, context_management, persistent ledger evidence, and progress_visualization.
answers.new_capability: headless.run.drive can accept an authorized journey_execution envelope, persist bounded execution checkpoints after committed Golden Journey boundaries, and replay or continue from those checkpoints without caller-supplied per-boundary route or closure envelopes.
answers.why_existing_functionality_is_insufficie: M50.4, M50.5, and M50.6 make approval, replacement, and closure safe one boundary at a time, but the caller still has to assemble drive ids, checkpoint fingerprints, route envelopes, and closure envelopes between process restarts.
answers.product_gap_if_skipped: A scheduled caller could prove every boundary in isolation but still could not invoke or recover a Golden Journey as one runtime-owned operation.
answers.non_duplicative: Distinct from M50.4 approval route resume, M50.5 replacement route resume, and M50.6 closure because it adds execution checkpointing and runtime-owned next-boundary selection across those already-merged capabilities.
answers.no_new_rpc: Yes. The phase extends existing headless.run.drive with a bounded journey_execution envelope and result metadata.
answers.no_new_summary: Yes. The phase adds execution behavior and checkpoint/result evidence, not a report, digest, history, readiness, verdict, inspection, preview, dashboard, or summary surface.
answers.runtime_behavior_change: Rust validates journey-execution authorization, admission or expected journey identity, current execution checkpoint freshness, unit budgets, mixed-field denials, persisted session and route evidence, and then delegates each next boundary under runtime authority before writing bounded execution checkpoints.
answers.headless_autonomous_contribution: A headless controller can retry the same authorized execution after an interrupted response and let the runtime return or continue from committed boundary evidence.
answers.milestone_progress: Moves M50 toward closeout by turning the individually safe Golden Journey boundaries into a restart-safe execution path.

guard_engine_change_review.review_intent: M50.7 updates the current and archived phase-value manifests for a product runtime Golden Journey execution phase. Review must confirm the manifest change does not weaken phase-value, product-completion, diagnostics, or source-of-truth enforcement.

exit_criteria: headless.run.drive accepts one authorized bounded journey_execution envelope without adding a new RPC
the runtime can admit a journey through journey_execution or continue an already-admitted journey from expected journey fingerprint evidence
journey execution persists bounded execution checkpoints after committed boundaries and reads them before replay or restart side effects
successful execution does not require caller-supplied journey_route_resume, journey_closure, or explicit Mode Pack target envelopes on the journey_execution path
replay or restart returns or continues from committed bounded metadata without duplicating task start, route-resume, replacement, finalization, closure, drive, or execution evidence

missing authorization, stale journey or execution fingerprint, mixed route or closure envelope, explicit Mode Pack target, completion-finalization bypass field, non-unit budget, and raw fields fail closed

VSIX validators accept the bounded journey_execution request and result shape and reject malformed fingerprints, false authorization, mixed envelopes, explicit targets, unbounded budgets, and raw fields
no report, digest, history, readiness, verdict, inspection, preview, dashboard, generic scheduler, broad runtime modularization, new RPC, or VSIX-owned policy is added
behavior_evidence: Rust behavior test headless_run_drive_journey_execution_admits_checkpoints_and_replays_without_new_task covers authorized journey_execution admission checkpointing, replay without a second task, bounded metadata, and raw-data exclusion.

Rust behavior test headless_run_drive_journey_route_resume_derives_fetch_provenance_and_approval_targets_and_replays remains passing and covers the M50 route/closure authorities reused by journey_execution.
VSIX runtimeClient protocol tests cover bounded journey_execution params and result metadata plus malformed, mixed, unbounded, and raw-field rejection.

accepted_capability: Runtime-owned headless Golden Journey execution checkpointing and restart replay through existing headless.run.drive
behavior_evidence: cargo test -p brownie-runtime headless_run_drive_journey -- --nocapture validates journey admission, execution admission checkpointing, route-resume regression, closure regression, replay, and denial behavior.
pnpm --filter brownie-vsix test -- runtimeClient.test.ts validates the journey_execution protocol guard shape.
cargo check -p brownie-runtime validates the Rust protocol, store, and runtime integration for the new checkpoint type.
safety_boundary: initial admission requires a bounded task_start and cannot include an expected journey fingerprint before the journey exists
post-admission continuation requires the expected journey fingerprint and may require the latest execution checkpoint fingerprint
journey_execution cannot mix journey_admission, journey_route_resume, journey_closure, explicit Mode Pack targets, context budgets, completion-finalization bypass fields, or non-unit budgets

RPC and ledger evidence is bounded to ids, enum values, hashes, fingerprints, counts, replay state, completion state, and next action; raw provenance material, Mode Pack payloads, prompts, provider responses, file content, command output, environment values, paths, and secrets are not returned or ledgered
non_goals: No report, digest, history, readiness, verdict, inspection, preview, dashboard, or summary wrapper
No generic scheduler, daemon, background worker, all-route workflow engine, or VSIX-owned policy
No automatic apply, recovery, provider, parent-join, shell, git, network, or service expansion
No behavior-preserving runtime-wide lib.rs modularization mixed into this product PR
rejected_alternatives: Adding a new headless.journey.execute RPC was rejected because existing headless.run.drive already owns bounded run-control authority.
Returning another readiness or execution preview was rejected because M50.7 must change runtime behavior and persist checkpoints.
Moving large sections of crates/brownie-runtime/src/lib.rs into modules was deferred because the phase must remain a cohesive product capability PR.
technical_debt: crates/brownie-runtime/src/lib.rs remains large and should be modularized later by cohesive low-dependency domains in independently buildable PRs.
The full selected-candidate route chain still depends on existing persisted Mode Pack selection evidence rather than adding a generic registry scheduler.
next_capability_rationale: If M50.7 completes review, M50 can move to milestone closeout because the remaining Golden Journey gap is runtime-owned execution and restart evidence rather than another isolated boundary.
